d2-cli.title: CLI startup and final export
d2-cli.alt: Tokio main parses Cli, translates configuration, awaits supervised trace_program, then exports bounded JSON separately; compilation failure may still produce a trace with exit code 2.

nodes.label: DebugSessionTrace
lines: May represent compile failure or partial run

d2-config.title: Configuration precedence and propagation
d2-config.alt: Default TraceConfig combines optional JSON configuration with supplied CLI scalar overrides and appended list options, then passes effective fields into compile, debugger, diagnostics and limits.
d2-config.caption: An omitted CLI scalar does not replace a JSON-configured value. Lists are appended where implemented; consult Cli::to_config for each flag.

d2-session.title: Supervised session state transitions
d2-session.alt: Session deadline wraps tool probe and compile, optional static metadata, one debugger stop loop, terminal heap verification, conditional separate diagnostics, final trace assembly and separate export.
d2-session.caption: Compile failure bypasses GDB; diagnostics are conditional; export happens after trace_program returns.

d2-error.title: Failure and retained evidence paths
d2-error.alt: Compiler failure yields a trace without debugger stops. GDB timeout or step cap can preserve partial observations. Missing ACK lowers heap completeness; export cap fails output without claiming a valid JSON document.
d2-error.caption: These outcomes are distinct: operational export error is not a successful partial exported trace.

d2-compile.title: GCC compilation subprocess lifecycle
d2-compile.alt: compile_project requests a wrapped debug build, then optionally combined or fallback ASan and UBSan builds; compile builds argv, supervises a GCC child, parses stderr and returns binary paths and diagnostics.
d2-compile.caption: Sanitizer build attempts are independent artifacts; a debug-build failure prevents GDB recording.

d2-build-artifacts.title: Source, executables and static metadata
d2-build-artifacts.alt: C source and embedded C wrapper are compiled into a GDB debug executable with DWARF. Optional ASan/UBSan executable is built separately without the wrapper; Clang AST is an independent static view.
d2-build-artifacts.caption: Dashed branches are separate artifacts or optional static analysis; neither syntax nor debug metadata is execution evidence.

d2-mi-cycle.title: MI token, result and asynchronous stop
d2-mi-cycle.alt: GdbSession assigns a command token and writes MI syntax to GDB stdin. Reader task parses stdout records, routes token-matched caret results to waiters and asynchronous stopped records separately; a command result is not a stop.

d2-mi-parse.title: MI record parsing pipeline
d2-mi-parse.alt: A complete GDB output line is tokenized with nom and parsed into result, asynchronous, notification or stream records; nested tuple and list values retain structure and unsupported classes rather than becoming observations.

d2-stop.title: Recorded debugger stop-loop choices
d2-stop.alt: At each observed stop, the loop ingests available heap lines before state capture. It chooses source checkpoint or instruction attempt from actual frame origin and mode, advances MI and waits for another stop; deadlines, signals and caps preserve gaps.
d2-stop.caption: A PC at a stop is the next attempted instruction; an acknowledgement alone cannot prove completion.

d2-checkpoint.title: Checkpoint construction from observed stop
d2-checkpoint.alt: Stop frame and selected variables are captured by GDB, pointer extents are qualified with observed maps and heap state, snapshot is retained by the recorder and a source-checkpoint index points at it.

d2-frame.title: Frames, variables and activation identity
d2-frame.alt: Selected frame and bounded caller frames produce scope-qualified variable records; activation identity distinguishes recursive frames even if names recur; unreadable values and bytes remain explicit partial observations.
d2-frame.caption: Frame activation is not a variable name, address, or inferred object lifetime.

d2-cache.title: Capture cache scope and invalidation
d2-cache.alt: Metadata and per-stop debugger probe results may be reused within their safe identity scope; a new stop, frame or module epoch prevents stale observations being treated as live data.
d2-cache.caption: Cache-safe scopes must be checked at implementation sites; this diagram makes no claim about reusing memory values across stops.

nodes.label: Static symbol/type metadata
lines: Compiled artifact, separate from live values

d2-memory.title: Memory read to evidence representation
d2-memory.alt: A selected observed variable supplies an address and extent; bounded debugger memory reads may be chunked or fail; recorder retains raw bytes and readability/truncation markers, without proving initialization.

d2-dwarf.title: ELF/DWARF CU and DIE traversal
d2-dwarf.alt: Extractor reads the GCC debug ELF, enumerates compilation units and DIEs, records type/member and declaration identities, then associates unique observed runtime declarations without interpreting DWARF location expressions.

nodes.label: Registry + association
lines: Static identities, runtime links only if unique

d2-origin.title: DWARF origin/specification reference chase
d2-origin.alt: A DIE reference may point within a CU or through DebugInfoRef to another CU. OriginResolver uses a four-hop bound and cycle detection; unresolved or ambiguous chains do not become declaration identity.

d2-ast.title: Optional Clang AST provider
d2-ast.alt: When enabled, bounded Clang invocation derives compatible flags from the GCC request, parses JSON AST declarations/expressions and retains source spans; unsupported preprocessing or missing tool leaves optional evidence unavailable.

nodes.label: AST registry
lines: Static syntax only; no execution proof

d2-ast-runtime.title: AST syntax is not runtime execution
d2-ast-runtime.alt: Clang source expression and GCC DWARF declaration may be linked as candidates through matching CU and source identity. A GDB checkpoint records live observations; a same-line expression alone is not a recorded executed call.
d2-ast-runtime.caption: Dashed arrows represent candidate metadata links, never definitive dynamic execution.

d2-wrapper.title: C allocation wrapper and event emission
d2-wrapper.alt: Linked --wrap allocator enters a recursion guard and spinlock, calls its real allocator exactly once, updates a fixed address-to-ID table on success, issues PID-local sequence and appends one event line.
d2-wrapper.caption: Only calls linked into the debug binary are intercepted; shared-library internals may bypass the wrapper.

nodes.label: Emit event line
lines: Unbuffered bounded write with failure count

nodes.label: Rust event reader
lines: Separate file transport, not Rust call

d2-transport.title: Allocation event and ACK transport
d2-transport.alt: C wrappers append PID/sequence-tagged event lines to a dedicated file; Rust tails only complete lines and checks per-observed-PID terminal ACKs from a separate status file. Missing or corrupt transport reduces completeness.

nodes.label: C wrapper event write
lines: PID, seq, kind, ID, address, size

d2-lifetimes.title: Heap event to allocation lifetime
d2-lifetimes.alt: Raw PID-local event sequence is validated before HeapTimeline creates or closes block state. Snapshot boundaries bracket heap events; final lifetime records retain source PCs and qualified completeness.

nodes.label: BlockState / lifetime
lines: Create, resize, free; retain event history

nodes.label: Checkpoint intervals
lines: Between retained observations, not exact stop

d2-realloc.title: Realloc outcomes and lifetime links
d2-realloc.alt: A failed realloc keeps its old block alive. Same-address success can retain a lifetime; moved success closes predecessor and creates successor with explicit old ID. Terminal realloc(ptr,0) may free without creating a successor.
d2-realloc.caption: Status and event identity, not numeric pointer equality, govern links; observed allocator behavior qualifies zero-size semantics.

d2-fork.title: Fork child and observed-PID scope
d2-fork.alt: An atfork child callback resets inherited lock and counters, deferring table clearing. Parent and logged child append PID-specific event lines and ACKs. An unlogged silent descendant is not known to the reader.
d2-fork.caption: A complete verified observed-PID history is not a process-tree census.

d2-diagnostics.title: Independent diagnostic provider orchestration
d2-diagnostics.alt: After primary GDB recording, Valgrind runs a separate Memcheck process; sanitizer pass may run earlier or later depending on crash trigger and availability. XML and stderr reports are retained separately from the primary execution.
d2-diagnostics.caption: No numeric primary-run allocation ID is proved by an independent diagnostic, even at the same source site.

d2-fusion.title: Bounded post-recording evidence fusion
d2-fusion.alt: GCC DWARF, optional Clang AST and existing runtime variables are indexed for source/declaration/type candidate links; heap call matching is site-only and final audit clears invalid references before publishing additive records.
d2-fusion.caption: Dashed bridges are static candidates. Fusion does not re-run GDB, prove an expression executed, or assign a primary allocation ID to Valgrind.

d2-model.title: Producer ownership of schema-2 records
d2-model.alt: Recorder owns captured checkpoints/instruction events, HeapTimeline owns native event history, static providers own metadata registries and diagnostics own separate reports; trace_program_inner assembles one DebugSessionTrace before main exports it.

d2-export.title: Counting preflight and atomic output
d2-export.alt: Exporter serializes once into a byte counter before file/stdout writing, rejects oversize final JSON, writes optional sibling temporary file and commits it before sending stdout; stdout I/O failure cannot undo committed file output.

d2-limits.title: Limits enforced at distinct boundaries
d2-limits.alt: Session deadline and subprocess output bounds, GDB step and capture limits, C event reader and journal caps, and JSON export cap are separate enforcement points; none is a global assembled trace RAM bound or sandbox.

d2-story-compile.title: Walkthrough A: source to debug executable
d2-story-compile.alt: CLI config selects C input, compiler builds GCC argument vector, supervisor captures bounded diagnostics, compile_project returns debug and optional sanitized artifacts.

d2-story-checkpoint.title: Walkthrough B: observed stop to checkpoint
d2-story-checkpoint.alt: GDB reader parses *stopped asynchronously, run_gdb_phase drains allocation events, captures frame and bounded variables, enriches pointers, and Recorder appends a snapshot and source checkpoint.

d2-story-malloc.title: Walkthrough C: malloc to lifetime
d2-story-malloc.alt: --wrap_malloc calls real allocator, updates PID-local fixed table, writes a line; Rust tailer reads complete events, HeapTimeline ingests a verified prefix and final assembly emits lifetimes.

d2-story-realloc.title: Walkthrough D: realloc outcomes
d2-story-realloc.alt: Wrapper's realloc result distinguishes failure, same-address success, moved success and observed terminal free. Rust history joins only recorded PID/sequence identities, never pointer equality alone.

d2-story-static.title: Walkthrough E: declaration metadata bridge
d2-story-static.alt: Dwarf extraction indexes a GCC declaration, optional Clang AST describes source syntax, evidence fusion uses CU and declaration identity to propose bounded links, and final trace retains unresolved/candidate status.

d2-story-failure.title: Walkthrough F: stop without complete run
d2-story-failure.alt: A crash, deadline or step cap ends the observed stop loop; supervisor cleans child groups, partial snapshots and gaps may survive, optional separate diagnostics can run within remaining budget and final export can independently fail its cap.
